 Denmark need only a point at Parken tomorrow night to reach the Nations League quarter-finals. Norway have to win, and if they do, the 3-2 win in Oslo in September puts them through on head-to-head.
 Brian Riemer's side arrive off a 4-1 win in Braga, while Ståle Solbakken's Norway beat Wales 3-1 on Saturday to keep the race alive. The goals markets expect another high-scoring game between them, but the chances in this group haven't matched the scorelines, and under 3.5 goals at 53¢ is where I see value.

 Denmark vs Norway Keys to the Game & Prediction Breakdown
 Analysis & Insights
 Denmark only need a point
 Denmark only need a point to progress after their stunning 4-1 win away in Portugal flipped the qualification script in their favorite. Norway won a thriller in Oslo in September, which gives them the edge on head-to-head, but any other result would send the Danes through behind group winners Portugal. Denmark can still top the group with a win here and an unlikely Wales win in Cardiff.
 Inflated scorelines due for regression
 Denmark's five group games have produced 19 goals from 13.36 total xG, and Norway's have produced 18 from 14.05. Denmark have scored 11 times from 7.62 xG. At the other end, Norway's two goalkeepers have conceded 3.03 more goals than the shots they've faced were worth. The biggest risk to this position in Erling Haaland. He scored twice from just 0.35 xG in Oslo.
 Value in the goals market
 Denmark are the slight favorites on prediction markets, priced at 40¢ at time of writing with Norway at 37¢. The ATS Quantitative Model largely agrees with the market, giving the hosts a 41.8% chance of winning to Norway's 33.4%, giving traders very little edge. However, there is value in the goals market. Over 3.5 goals has been pumped up to 48¢ thanks to Denmark's goalscoring form, leaving under 3.5 goals at 53¢. Our model sees plenty of value here, giving the under a 61.4% chance, leaving a 8.4% edge.

 “ Denmark games have seen plenty of goals in this Nations League campaign, and the market has reacted accordingly. However, the goal gluts in Oslo and Braga saw 10 goals scored from a cumulative 5.93 xG, and half of those came from set pieces or penalties. In Oslo these two sides only registered 2.5 xG between them, and the Danes in particular can't continue socring at this clip given the lack of quality chances they're producing. The hosts only need a draw, so I don’t see them opening up at Parken. ”
 — Simon Cripps • Sports Analyst

 Denmark have given up more big chances than they've created, and six of the 13 came in the 4-2 home defeat to Portugal in October.
 Norway's defensive numbers include 44 minutes with ten men in Cardiff, after Torbjørn Heggem was sent off a minute after half-time in the 2-1 defeat to Wales.
 The two sides are almost identical on the ball. Neither has averaged more than 52% possession, and the gap in xG/90 is just 0.11.
 Tactical Analysis Denmark's goals have come from dead balls far more than open play. Seven of their 11 have been set pieces or penalties, including Joachim Andersen's header in Braga. Norway have conceded from a corner, two free kicks and a throw-in routine in this group, so every Denmark set piece at Parken is a threat.
 In open play, Denmark build through Andersen. He's made 54 passes into the final third from centre-back, more than double his partner Oliver Provstgaard. Further forward, Mohamed Daramy gives them a second dribbler alongside Isaksen, with 12 successful dribbles and 28 touches in the box.
 Norway's problem is the space around Ødegaard. Morten Hjulmand and Pierre-Emile Højbjerg will sit in front of the back four, and Højbjerg's job is to stop Ødegaard turning between the lines. If he can't get on the ball facing goal, Haaland's supply dries up, and Norway's next-best route is Nusa running at Denmark's right-back.
 Game state should slow this down. Denmark don't need to win, so they can let Norway have the ball and look to break through Højlund, who scored on the counter in the home defeat to Portugal. Norway have to commit numbers at some point, but pushing too early against a side that breaks this quickly is a risk Solbakken may not take. If it's level going into the last half hour, Norway will push, but by then there's less time for the game to open up.
 Key Numbers & Trends Haaland scored twice in Norway's 3-2 win in Oslo in September, including the winner from a corner in the 74th minute.
 In the five meetings before September, going back to 2011, Denmark won three and drew two.
 Both sides have scored in all five of their group games.
 Five of Norway's nine group goals have come from set pieces or penalties.
 Mads Hermansen has made 14 saves in his three group games for Denmark.
